rule_as_specified.candidate_section: ATX heading AND not numeric AND not TOC AND not URL/copyright AND length <= 140
rule_as_specified.section_level: shallowest level with at least 2 surviving headings
rule_as_specified.classification: NORMAL if at least 2 sections, DEGENERATE if fewer than 2
rule_as_specified.semantics: syntactic partitioning only; no judgement whether something really is a section

implementation_bugs_found_and_corrected: Sections were first split at every heading of the chosen level or deeper, including headings already rejected as artefacts. The rule requires rejected headings to be plain text, not split points. On the ILO guide this produced 331 sections from 77 surviving candidates. Corrected to split only at surviving candidates of the chosen level; split_consistency_ok is now true for all 18 documents.
ATX.finditer(cut, re.M) passed the re.M integer as the `pos` argument rather than as a flag, so the census started at offset 8 and reported zero headings. Corrected to a re.M-compiled pattern.
An earlier pass (v1) profiled clean() output, in which heading lines have already been deleted, and reported zero headings corpus-wide. Headings must be read from the raw snapshot.

summary.interpretation: a high largest_section_ratio is a measurable property of the source, not an error. USGS MCS2025 at 0.854 and the sustainability EO at 0.732 are reports whose usable text is genuinely concentrated in a few sections. It is reported, not corrected.
summary.note_on_deeper_levels: h3 and deeper never occur in this corpus, and headings below the chosen level become inline text inside their parent section
